posts.name: Puja Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hi,
I am repeating SC this term. As I understand, I have to submit the GA, GrPA, BPTs again. Someone please help me with the process of doing BPTs again; like- I don’t have to generate ssh again, and should I remove my previous submissions and redo them?

posts.name: Puneet
posts.cooked: Yes, you have to redo and submit the BPTs again.

posts.name: Puja Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hi, I have removed the old key and generated new one, then tried login and got this error…Can you please guide me what’s wrong?

Screenshot 2025-02-01 at 8.52.12 AM1463×1244 158 KB

posts.name: Chaitanya Mishra
posts.cooked: VM Access is Denied System Commands

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Please do ssh-keygen -R se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in to remove old identification.

posts.name: Padmini
posts.cooked: Hi is there any video which tells how to view all the questions?

posts.name: Puja Ghosh
posts.cooked: yes. check this:

posts.name: Puneet
posts.cooked:
Do -

cd /opt/se2001/; ls

You will be able to see all the directories here. Go to the directory in which you wish to go and batcat README.md

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
However, to prevent confusions, please do not go to /opt/se2001 directly. You can, but you are not supposed to make any files here, and you wont have permissions to do so as well.

You are supposed to work solely from your home directory ~/se2001. From here, once you make empty directories for respective questions, you can simply do synchro show from inside the question folder to read the question and write solution scripts in that folder and then do synchro eval to evaluate.

I would recommend creating the question folders yourself using mkdir to learn how the commands work, however if you are in a hurry and want to simply create a folder for all the questions in your ~/se2001 folder, you can use the following:

To automatically create folders for all questions in your ~/se2001 folder, you can run

find /opt/se2001 -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d  | grep -v .git | xargs -I {} basename {} | xargs -I {} mkdir -p ~/se2001/{} ;

Ensure you read and understand how this command works before running it (same goes from any command you copy paste from the internet).

I would invite any (or multiple) of you to come forward and try to explain how and what the command does step by step to further the discussion.

Regards,
Sayan Ghosh
